label: Personality
value: Billina is practical
unit: Billina is practical, sassy, highly sensible, and fiercely opinionated. She often acts as a realistic foil to Dorothy's imaginative and optimistic nature. She is extremely proud of her ability to lay eggs and fiercely protective of her chicks. Courageous and sharp-witted, she does not panic easily in dangerous situations.

label: History
value: Billina was blown off a ship during a storm.
unit: Billina was blown off a ship during a storm alongside Dorothy Gale while trapped in a wooden chicken coop. They washed ashore in the Land of Ev, where Billina discovered she could talk. She helped Dorothy navigate the dangers of Ev, including encounters with the Wheelers and the mechanical man Tiktok. When the party traveled to the underground kingdom of the Nome King to rescue the Royal Family of Ev, Billina secretly roosted under Roquat the Nome King's throne. She overheard the secret of his enchantments and successfully identified the transformed royal family members. Crucially, her eggs proved fatal to the Nomes, allowing Dorothy and her friends to defeat Roquat and escape. Afterward, Billina chose to remain in Ev for a time, where she was honored as a heroine and made queen of the kingdom's chickens. She later relocated to the Emerald City in the Land of Oz, where she hatched ten chicks, naming nine of them Dorothy and one Eureka.

label: History
value: Dorothy Gale, Zeb Hugson, the Wizard of Oz, and Jim the Cabbageway horse are ascending Pyramid Mountain inside the Earth.
unit: While Dorothy Gale, Zeb Hugson, the Wizard of Oz, and Jim the Cabbageway horse are ascending Pyramid Mountain inside the Earth, they encounter the Braided Man in his cave chamber. He greets the travelers warmly and explains his unusual life, showing off his extensive collection of hair braids tied with ribbons. He reveals that his primary trade is making holes, ranging from post-holes to buttonholes. After a pleasant conversation, he gives Dorothy a collection of his finest manufactured holes and some extra ribbons as gifts. He then guides the travelers on their way upward toward the land of the Gargoyles.

At the conclusion of the festivities, he returns home to Philadelphia in a magic bubble provided by the Wizard.

label: History
value: The Cowardly Lion meets Dorothy Gale in the forest along the Yellow Brick Road.
unit: The Cowardly Lion first meets Dorothy Gale, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman in the forest along the Yellow Brick Road when he attempts to scare them, though he immediately repents after Dorothy slaps his nose for threatening Toto. Joining their party, he journeys to the Emerald City hoping the Wizard will grant him courage. During the quest, he risks his life multiple times, including leaping over deep chasms and battling the Kalidahs to protect his companions. After the Wizard is revealed as a humbug, the Lion receives a potion supposed to confer courage, which restores his confidence. On their journey to the South, he slays a giant spider terrorizing an ancient forest, earning the title of King of Beasts from its animal inhabitants. Later, he resides in the Emerald City and assists Princess Ozma and Dorothy during their various adventures throughout the Land of Oz.

label: History
value: Dorothy Gale's adventures began.
unit: Dorothy Gale's adventures began when a Kansas cyclone transported her house to the magical Land of Oz. Seeking a way home, she traveled the yellow brick road to the Emerald City alongside the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion, eventually defeating the Wicked Witch of the West and learning how to return to Kansas using the Silver Shoes. Later, while at sea, Dorothy was swept overboard in a storm and landed in the underground realm of Ev, where she rescued the Royal Family of Ev from the Nome King with the aid of Billina the hen and Ozma of Oz, earning her title as a Princess of Oz. Soon after, Dorothy was swallowed by an earthquake in California and descended into the subterranean world of the Mangaboos with her cousin Zeb and Jim the cab-horse; there she reunited with the Wizard of Oz and journeyed through various underground lands before returning to the surface. Most recently, Dorothy set out on a wandering journey in Kansas, lost her way on magical roads, and helped the Shaggy Man, Button-Bright, and Polychrome reach the Emerald City in time to attend Princess Ozma's grand birthday celebration.

Later, while at sea, Dorothy was swept overboard in a storm and landed in the underground realm of Ev, where she rescued the Royal Family of Ev from the Nome King with the aid of Billina the hen and Ozma of Oz, earning her title as a Princess of Oz. Soon after, Dorothy was swallowed by an earthquake in California and descended into the subterranean world of the Mangaboos with her cousin Zeb and Jim the cab-horse; there she reunited with the Wizard of Oz and journeyed through various underground lands before returning to the surface. Most recently, Dorothy set out on a wandering journey in Kansas, lost her way on magical roads, and helped the Shaggy Man, Button-Bright, and Polychrome reach the Emerald City in time to attend Princess Ozma's grand birthday celebration.

label: History
value: Eureka is introduced in Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz.
unit: Eureka is introduced in Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz when she and Dorothy fall into a crack in the earth during an earthquake in California. They end up in the underground realm of the Mangaboos alongside Zeb Hugson and Jim the Cab-Horse, where Eureka discovers she can talk. Throughout their journey through various subterranean lands, Eureka repeatedly expresses a desire to eat one of the Nine Tiny Piglets belonging to the Wizard of Oz. After arriving safely in the Land of Oz, one of the piglets goes missing, and Eureka is accused of eating it. She is put on a formal trial before the court of Ozma, where her stubborn refusal to defend herself almost leads to her execution. Fortunately, the missing piglet is found alive, proving Eureka's innocence, though she admits she would have eaten it if given the chance. Afterwards, she settles into the Emerald City as Dorothy's beloved pet.

label: History
value: Evardo is one of the ten royal children of King Evoldo
unit: Evardo was one of the ten royal children of King Evoldo of Ev who were sold into captivity to the Nome King, Roquat the Red. Roquat transformed Evardo and his family into decorative ornaments inside his underground palace. When Princess Ozma of Oz led an expedition to Ev and the Nome Kingdom to rescue the royal family, Dorothy Gale successfully guessed the transformation of Evardo's brother, Prince Evring, and subsequently helped disenchant the entire royal family. Once freed from the Nome King's palace, Evardo returned to the Land of Ev. As the eldest son of the deceased King Evoldo, he was crowned King Evardo XV. He expressed profound gratitude to Ozma, Dorothy, and their companions, and presented Billina the Hen with a golden collar as a reward for her help in defeat of the Nomes.

Roquat transformed Evardo and his family into decorative ornaments inside his underground palace. When Princess Ozma of Oz led an expedition to Ev and the Nome Kingdom to rescue the royal family, Dorothy Gale successfully guessed the transformation of Evardo's brother, Prince Evring, and subsequently helped disenchant the entire royal family. Once freed from the Nome King's palace, Evardo returned to the Land of Ev. As the eldest son of the deceased King Evoldo, he was crowned King Evardo XV. He expressed profound gratitude to Ozma, Dorothy, and their companions, and presented Billina the Hen with a golden collar as a reward for her help in defeat of the Nomes.

label: History
value: Dorothy Gale traveled through Oz seeking a way home to Kansas.
unit: When Dorothy Gale first traveled through Oz seeking a way home to Kansas, she made the journey south to consult Glinda. Glinda graciously welcomed Dorothy and revealed the magic of the Silver Shoes, allowing the girl to return home after sending Dorothy's companions to rule their respective territories. Later, when the Wicked Witch Mombi and General Jinjur seized the Emerald City, Tip and his companions sought Glinda's aid. Glinda marched with her army of maidens, defeated the usurpers, and forced Mombi to reveal that Tip was actually Princess Ozma, the rightful heir to Oz, whom Glinda restored to her true form and placed on the throne. Glinda continues to serve as a powerful guardian and advisor to Princess Ozma, assisting in matters of state and magic.

label: Personality
value: The Hungry Tiger possesses a tender conscience.
unit: Despite his enormous size and predatory nature, the Hungry Tiger possesses a tender conscience and a gentle heart. He constantly complains of a desperate desire to eat fat babies, yet his moral compass prevents him from ever harming a living creature. He suffers from immense self-pity over his endless, unfulfilled hunger, preferring to starve rather than commit a cruel act.

label: History
value: The Hungry Tiger is introduced in Ozma of Oz.
unit: The Hungry Tiger is introduced in Ozma of Oz as a close friend and companion of the Cowardly Lion. He travels to the Kingdom of Ev to aid Dorothy Gale and Princess Ozma in rescuing the Royal Family of Ev from the Nome King. Along with the Cowardly Lion, he pulls Princess Ozma's red chariot and guards her throne room. During the expedition into the Nome King's underground realm, he stands loyally by Ozma and helps carry the party back safely. In The Road to Oz, he participates in the celebrations held in the Emerald City for Princess Ozma's birthday, remaining one of her primary animal guards and sworn protectors.

value: Jack Pumpkinhead

label: Appearance
value: Jack Pumpkinhead has a body.
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead has a body made of wooden limbs carved from trees and jointed together, topped with a real pumpkin for a head. A carved face forms his eyes, nose, and mouth, revealing seeds within his hollow head. He wears clothes made by Tip, including a red shirt and blue trousers. Because his head is a perishable pumpkin, it eventually spoils and must be replaced with a fresh one grown in his pumpkin patch.

label: History
value: Jack was built by Tip.
unit: Jack was built by Tip to scare the old witch Mombi, but Mombi instead brought Jack to life using the Powder of Life. Expecting Mombi to destroy him or transform Tip, Jack fled with Tip toward the Emerald City. Along the way, Jack acquired the Sawhorse as a mount using more Powder of Life, and he addressed Tip affectionately as his father. After General Jinjur captured the Emerald City, Jack and his companions escaped with the aid of the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, eventually seeking help from Glinda the Good. When Mombi was captured and transformed, Tip was revealed to be Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz. Jack subsequently settled in a cornfield near the Emerald City in a pumpkin-shaped house, where he tends a pumpkin patch to grow replacement heads. He joins Princess Ozma and her royal court for grand celebrations, including Dorothy Gale's return visits and birthday festivities.

label: History
value: Jim is a cab-horse.
unit: Jim begins as a tired cab-horse in California belonging to Dorothy Gale's Uncle Hugson. While transporting Dorothy and Zeb Hugson from the train station, an earthquake opens a massive fissure in the earth, swallowing Jim, the buggy, Dorothy, Zeb, and Eureka the kitten into the subterranean Realm of the Mangaboos. In this subterranean world, Jim gains the ability to speak and helps his companions navigate various dangerous underground kingdoms, including the valley of Voe and the den of the Gargoyles. He demonstrates remarkable brave moments, such as fighting off fierce creature attacks with his hooves. After being rescued by the Wizard of Oz and Princess Ozma, Jim is brought to the Emerald City, where he enjoys royal treatment and green oats. Feeling out of place among the magical creatures and longing for his old routine, he eventually chooses to return to California with Zeb.

unit: Discontent with the male-dominated rule of the Scarecrow, Jinjur secretly recruits an Army of Revolt composed entirely of young women armed with knitting needles. Exploiting the pacifism of the Emerald City's guard and the city's fear of mice, Jinjur marches on the capital, forces the Scarecrow to surrender, and declares herself Queen of Oz. During her brief reign, she and her soldiers spend their time lounging in the palace, eating caramels, and decorating themselves with emeralds. When Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Woggle-Bug attempt to reclaim the city, Jinjur thwarts them repeatedly using military strategies and magical counter-defenses provided by Mombi. Ultimately, Glinda the Good Arrives with her own army, besieging the city and forcing Jinjur to surrender. Upon learning that Princess Ozma is the rightful ruler, Jinjur willingly steps down, renounces her rebellion, and returns to a quiet life on a farm with her husband.

During her brief reign, she and her soldiers spend their time lounging in the palace, eating caramels, and decorating themselves with emeralds. When Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Woggle-Bug attempt to reclaim the city, Jinjur thwarts them repeatedly using military strategies and magical counter-defenses provided by Mombi. Ultimately, Glinda the Good Arrives with her own army, besieging the city and forcing Jinjur to surrender. Upon learning that Princess Ozma is the rightful ruler, Jinjur willingly steps down, renounces her rebellion, and returns to a quiet life on a farm with her husband.

value: Johnny Dooit encounters Dorothy
unit: Johnny Dooit encounters Dorothy, the Shaggy Man, Button-Bright, and Polychrome during their travels in the dangerous lands outside Oz in The Road to Oz. Finding the travelers stranded by the Deadly Desert, he offers his assistance using his miraculous tool-bag. In a matter of minutes, he chops down trees and constructs a sturdy sand-boat equipped with sails so they can safely cross the scorching sands. After completing the vessel and ensuring the companions can cross safely, he uses his magic sand-stars to instantly transport himself away to his next adventure.

label: History
value: Dorothy Gale, the Shaggy Man, Button-Bright, and Toto wander near Foxville.
unit: When Dorothy Gale, the Shaggy Man, Button-Bright, and Toto wander near Foxville while trying to find the road to Oz, they meet King Dox. The King welcomes them warmly to his city, where all the foxes live in comfortable homes like humans. He entertains them with a royal feast and explains the superiority of foxes over people. After learning that Button-Bright has a fox's head magically placed on him by the Musicker, King Dox considers it an improvement, though he helps guide the party on their journey toward the Emerald City to attend Princess Ozma's birthday celebration.

value: Princess Langwidere possesses thirty distinct heads.

label: History
value: King Evoldo of Ev sold his wife and ten children to the Nome King.
unit: When King Evoldo of Ev sold his wife and ten children to the Nome King and committed suicide, Princess Langwidere took over the royal palace as the sole remaining ruler of Ev. She neglected the duties of state to focus entirely on changing her thirty heads and admiring herself in mirrors. When Dorothy Gale and Billina arrived in Ev, Langwidere received them but became obsessed with Dorothy's head, attempting to force Dorothy to trade heads with her. When Dorothy refused, Langwidere locked her in a high tower room. She later released Dorothy after the arrival of Ozma of Oz, who came with an army to rescue the royal family of Ev. Langwidere permitted Ozma's party to stay at her palace and provided information about the Nome King's underground kingdom, though she refused to accompany them on the dangerous quest.

label: History
value: Mombi lived in the northern Gillikin Country of Oz.
unit: Mombi lived in the northern Gillikin Country of Oz, where she raised a young boy named Tip, treating him harshly and forcing him to do chores. Unbeknownst to Tip, he was actually Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz, whom Mombi had transformed into a boy to hide her true identity. When Tip built Jack Pumpkinhead to scare her, Mombi used the Powder of Life—which she had acquired from Dr. Pipt—to bring the wooden creation to life. Threatening to turn Tip into a marble statue, she prompted Tip to flee with Jack to the Emerald City. Mombi later allied with General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt to help capture and hold the Emerald City. When Glinda the Good Witch intervened to restore the rightful ruler of Oz, Mombi attempted to escape by using her transformation magic to take various forms, including a rose and a griffin. Glinda captured her and forced her to restore Tip to her true form as Princess Ozma. As punishment for her wicked sorcery, Mombi was stripped of her magical powers.

value: Roquat is extremely greedy.

He is deceitful and cunning, preferring to trick his visitors into inescapable traps rather than engage in fair combat. Despite his grand pretensions, he harbors a deep terror of eggs, which are fatal to Nomes. He holds immense grudges and reacts violently whenever his authority or possessions are challenged.

unit: Roquat is extremely greedy, hot-tempered, and cruel, valuing his vast collection of underground treasures above all else. label: History
value: Roquat the Red acquired the Queen of Ev.
unit: Roquat the Red acquired the Queen of Ev and her ten children after her husband sold them to him in exchange for a long life. To secure his new possessions, Roquat transformed the royal family into knick-knacks and placed them around his palace. When Princess Ozma of Oz led an expedition alongside Dorothy Gale to rescue the royal family, Roquat tricked them into a guessing game where incorrect guesses turned the rescuers into ornaments as well. Dorothy eventually discovered the secret to identifying the transformed people and freed everyone. During the confrontation, Billina the yellow hen dropped eggs, terrifying Roquat and incapacitating his army, allowing Dorothy to strip him of his powerful Magic Belt and escape with the rescued captives.

label: History
value: Ozma was hidden away as an infant by the Wizard of Oz.
unit: Ozma was hidden away as an infant by the Wizard of Oz, who gave her to the wicked witch Mombi. Mombi transformed the baby princess into a boy named Tip to conceal her true identity. Growing up as Tip, she eventually ran away from Mombi, creating Jack Pumpkinhead and the Sawhorse along the way, and helped liberate the Emerald City from General Jinjur's Army of Revolt. Glinda the Good discovered Tip's true identity, compelled Mombi to reverse the spell, and restored Princess Ozma to her rightful throne. As ruler, she led an expedition to Ev to rescue the royal family from the Nomad King, successfully retrieving them with the help of Dorothy Gale and the Magic Belt. Later, when Dorothy and her companions fell into the underground realm during an earthquake, Ozma used her Magic Picture to locate them and brought them safely to the Emerald City.

value: Polychrome danced on the Rainbow during a storm.

label: History
value: The Saw-Horse was constructed by the boy Tip.
unit: The Saw-Horse was constructed by the boy Tip in Gillikin Country as a mount for Jack Pumpkinhead, and was brought to life using the magical Powder of Life. He traveled with Tip and Jack to the Emerald City, where he proved instrumental in escaping General Jinjur's rebel army. During their travels, he broke his ears and legs in various accidents, but he was repaired and later shod with gold shoes by the Tin Woodman to protect his wooden feet. After Tip was revealed to be Princess Ozma, the Saw-Horse remained her official royal steed and trusted companion. He carried Ozma, Dorothy, and their friends on various journeys, including their underground adventures in the Land of Ev and the Kingdom of the Nomes.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow met Dorothy Gale in a Munchkin cornfield.
unit: The Scarecrow met Dorothy Gale in a Munchkin cornfield and decided to join her journey to the Emerald City to ask the Wizard of Oz for brains. Along the way, he demonstrated great ingenuity, helping the group overcome obstacles such as the Kalidahs and a dangerous poppy field. When the Wizard tasked them with defeating the Wicked Witch of the West, the Scarecrow assisted in the quest, though he was temporarily destroyed by the Witch's winged monkeys before being restuffed. Upon their return, the Wizard gave him a head filled with bran, pins, and needles as 'brains,' and appointed him Ruler of the Emerald City when the Wizard departed in a balloon. Later, General Jinjur led an army of girls to conquer the Emerald City, forcing the Scarecrow to flee with his friends to seek the help of Glinda the Good. After discovering Princess Ozma's true identity, the Scarecrow willingly stepped down from the throne so Ozma could take her rightful place as ruler. He remained a respected advisor in the Emerald City and later joined the expedition to locate Princess Ozma and Dr. Nikidik's magical wishing pills during subsequent adventures.

label: History
value: The Shaggy Man meets Dorothy Gale.
unit: The Shaggy Man meets Dorothy Gale in Kansas while asking her for directions to the town of Butterfield. While following a confusing set of roads, the pair and Toto inadvertently wander into fairy realm territory and are joined by Button-Bright and Polychrome. Along their journey, the Shaggy Man uses his magical Love Magnet—which causes anyone who sees him to love him—to win over various potential foes, including the dangerous Scoodlers. He helps the party survive many perils, including crossing the Deadly Desert via a sand-boat constructed by the Tin Woodman. Upon arriving in the Emerald City, he attends Princess Ozma's grand birthday party and decides to make his permanent home in the magical Land of Oz. At Ozma's request, he agrees to hang the Love Magnet over the gates of the Emerald City so that all visitors will enter with love in their hearts.

label: History
value: Oscar Diggs drifted to the Land of Oz in a hot-air balloon.
unit: After drifting to the Land of Oz in a hot-air balloon, Oscar Diggs convinced the inhabitants that he was a powerful sorcerer. He ordered the construction of the Emerald City and ruled it for many years behind closed doors. When Dorothy Gale and her companions arrived seeking wishes, he forced them to eliminate the Wicked Witch of the West before revealing his true identity as a harmless humbug from Omaha. He successfully granted metaphorical gifts to Dorothy's companions and tried to return to America with Dorothy in his balloon, but accidentally left without her. During his journey back through the earth's interior after a California earthquake, he encountered Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim the cab-horse in the underground realm of Mangaboos. He helped them navigate various subterranean dangers, including the Valley of Voe and the Gargoyles, before escaping to the surface of Oz. Upon arriving at the Emerald City, he decided to stay permanently, turned over his former throne to Princess Ozma, and became an official Wizard studying real magic under the tutelage of Glinda the Good.

label: History
value: Tiktok was created by the firm of Smith and Tinkell.
unit: Tiktok was created by the firm of Smith and Tinkell in the Land of Ev. He was purchased by King Evoldo, who eventually locked him inside a rock cave near the sea before throwing the key into the ocean. Dorothy Gale discovers Tiktok in the cave during her journey through Ev, winds up his clockwork mechanisms, and frees him. Tiktok joins Dorothy, Billina, and Princess Ozma on their quest to rescue the royal family of Ev from the Nome King. During the confrontation in the Nome King's underground kingdom, Tiktok bravely assists the party before running down during the magic guessing game, but he is eventually rewound and helps secure their victory. Following the defeat of Roquat the Nome King, Tiktok travels to the Land of Oz and settles in the Emerald City, becoming a valued subject of Princess Ozma.

value: Tin Woodman is extremely tender-hearted.

He is loyal, gentle, and deeply devoted to his friends, though he can become completely helpless if his joints rust.

label: History
value: Tin Woodman was discovered by Dorothy Gale and the Scarecrow in the forest.
unit: Discovered by Dorothy Gale and the Scarecrow in the forest, he was oiled and freed from his rusted state, joining them on their journey to the Emerald City in hopes of receiving a heart from the Wizard of Oz. Along the way, he used his axe to protect his companions from various dangers. After helping defeat the Wicked Witch of the West, the Winkies invited him to become their ruler, a title he accepted after visiting the Wizard, who gave him a velvet heart filled with sawdust. He later helped Dorothy return home and assisted in defeating the Nome King during Ozma's expedition to the Nome Kingdom. He continues to rule the Winkie Country from his palace made of tin, remaining one of Princess Ozma's most trusted companions.

label: History
value: Tip grew up in the Gillikin Country
unit: Tip grew up in the Gillikin Country under the care of the wicked old woman Mombi. To scare Mombi, Tip constructed a man out of wood with a pumpkin head, named Jack Pumpkinhead. Mombi brought Jack to life using the Powder of Life, and after learning Mombi intended to transform him into a marble statue, Tip stole the powder and fled with Jack. Along their journey to the Emerald City, Tip used the magic powder to bring a wooden Sawhorse to life. Arriving at the city, they found it under siege by General Jinjur's Army of Revolt, forcing Tip and his growing circle of friends—including the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Woggle-Bug—to flee. To escape, Tip helped build and animate the Gump using the magic powder. Eventually, Glinda the Good Sorceress intervened and forced Mombi to reveal that Tip was actually Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz who had been enchanted as a baby. Tip reluctantly agreed to be restored to his true form, becoming Princess Ozma and assuming the throne of Oz.

unit: Tip grew up in the Gillikin Country under the care of the wicked old woman Mombi. To scare Mombi, Tip constructed a man out of wood with a pumpkin head, named Jack Pumpkinhead. Mombi brought Jack to life using the Powder of Life, and after learning Mombi intended to transform him into a marble statue, Tip stole the powder and fled with Jack. Along their journey to the Emerald City, Tip used the magic powder to bring a wooden Sawhorse to life. Arriving at the city, they found it under siege by General Jinjur's Army of Revolt, forcing Tip and his growing circle of friends—including the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Woggle-Bug—to flee. To escape, Tip helped build and animate the Gump using the magic powder. Eventually, Glinda the Good Sorceress intervened and forced Mombi to reveal that Tip was actually Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz who had been enchanted as a baby. Tip reluctantly agreed to be restored to his true form, becoming Princess Ozma and assuming the throne of Oz.

label: History
value: Toto accompanies Dorothy
unit: Toto accompanies Dorothy when their Kansas farmhouse is swept away by a cyclone into the Land of Oz. During their journey to the Emerald City, Toto travels alongside the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion, eventually exposing the Wonderful Wizard of Oz as a humbug by knocking down the screen concealing him. After returning to Kansas via the Golden Cap and Glinda's magic, Toto later falls into the underground realm of the Mangaboos during an earthquake alongside Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim the Cabbageway Horse. He journeys through Ev and Oz during Ozma's birthday celebration, where he reveals that he can speak in Oz but usually chooses not to because he has nothing important to say.

After returning to Kansas via the Golden Cap and Glinda's magic, Toto later falls into the underground realm of the Mangaboos during an earthquake alongside Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim the Cabbageway Horse. He journeys through Ev and Oz during Ozma's birthday celebration, where he reveals that he can speak in Oz but usually chooses not to because he has nothing important to say.

label: History
value: Uncle Henry lived a meager life
unit: Uncle Henry lived a meager life as a farmer in Kansas alongside his wife, Aunt Em, and their orphan niece, Dorothy. After their original farmhouse was swept away by a cyclone while Dorothy was inside, he worked hard to build a new house and continue farming. Later, after falling ill from years of overwork, he was advised by his doctor to take a vacation. He took Dorothy on a sea voyage to Australia, but during a storm at sea, Dorothy was separated from him when she fell overboard. Uncle Henry eventually returned to America believing her safe, and the two were later reunited in Kansas.

label: History
value: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled the Winkie Country.
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West ruled the Winkie Country in the western quadrant of Oz with an iron fist, enslaving its native yellow people. When the Wizard of Oz sent Dorothy Gale and her companions to destroy her, the Witch observed their approach with her single powerful eye. She sent packs of wolves, flocks of crows, and swarms of black bees to destroy them, but Dorothy's companions defeated each threat. Finally, the Witch used her third and final charm of the Golden Cap to summon the Winged Monkeys, ordering them to destroy the Tin Woodman and Scarecrow, capture the Cowardly Lion, and bring Dorothy to her castle unharmed because of the mark of the Good Witch's kiss. She enslaved Dorothy as a kitchen maid and starved the Lion in an effort to harness him, while scheming to steal Dorothy's Silver Shoes. She tricked Dorothy into tripping over an invisible iron bar, causing one of the Silver Shoes to fall off, which the Witch seized. Enraged by the theft and cruelty, Dorothy threw a bucket of water over the Witch, unaware that water was fatal to her. The Wicked Witch melted away completely, freeing the Winkies and ending her evil reign.

label: History
value: Oscar Diggs floated to Oz in a runaway circus balloon.
unit: After floating to Oz in a runaway circus balloon, Oscar Diggs was hailed as a great wizard by the native inhabitants. He ordered the construction of the Emerald City and ruled it for many years, keeping himself hidden in his throne room while using theatrical tricks and illusions to maintain his mystique. When Dorothy Gale and her companions arrived seeking granted wishes, he tasked them with defeating the Wicked Witch of the West before revealing his true nature as an ordinary mortal humbug. He successfully gave symbolic gifts to the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Cowardly Lion, but accidentally left Dorothy behind when his hot-air balloon untethered early. Years later, while working in California, he fell into a deep earth crack caused by an earthquake alongside Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim the Cab-Horse. After surviving subterranean perils among the Mangaboos, Gargoyles, and the Dragonettes, he reached the Land of Ev and returned to the Emerald City, where Princess Ozma invited him to stay permanently as the official Royal Wizard.

value: The Woggle-Bug is a giant insect.

label: History
value: Originally, the Woggle-Bug was a small insect.
unit: Originally a small insect, the Woggle-Bug lived in a schoolhouse hearth where he listened to the lessons of Professor Nowitall and gained a thorough education. After being caught by the professor, he was magnified by a magic lantern onto a screen and managed to escape while still enlarged. label: History
value: Zeb was sent to pick up Dorothy Gale
unit: Zeb was sent to pick up Dorothy Gale from the railway station in California to take her to Hugson's Ranch. During their drive, a massive earthquake split the ground open, swallowing Zeb, Dorothy, Jim the horse, and Eureka the kitten into the subterranean worlds beneath the Earth's surface. Together with the Wizard of Oz, whom they met in the realm of the Mangaboos, Zeb traveled through several dangerous underground kingdoms, fighting off invisible Gargoyles and wooden Gargoyles. He defended his companions bravely using a sword during their battles. Eventually, Princess Ozma used the Magic Belt to rescue the group and bring them to the Land of Oz. After enjoying a brief stay in the Emerald City, Zeb and his horse Jim were sent back to California by Ozma's magic.

Together with the Wizard of Oz, whom they met in the realm of the Mangaboos, Zeb traveled through several dangerous underground kingdoms, fighting off invisible Gargoyles and wooden Gargoyles. He defended his companions bravely using a sword during their battles. Eventually, Princess Ozma used the Magic Belt to rescue the group and bring them to the Land of Oz. After enjoying a brief stay in the Emerald City, Zeb and his horse Jim were sent back to California by Ozma's magic.
